content.rendered:
These bars set in the fridge with no gelatin, thanks to cream cheese and whipped cream. Make them the day before a party and just slice and serve.

Prep: 20 min · Cook: 6 hours chilling · Serves: 12 bars

Ingredients

  • 200 g digestive biscuits
  • 80 g butter, melted
  • 400 g cream cheese, softened
  • 1/2 cup icing sugar
  • Zest and juice of 2 lemons
  • 1 cup cold whipping cream

Method

  1. Crush the biscuits, mix with the melted butter and press into a lined 20 cm tin. Chill 15 minutes.
  2. Beat the cream cheese, icing sugar, lemon zest and juice until smooth.
  3. Whip the cream to stiff peaks and fold it into the cream cheese mix.
  4. Spread over the base and smooth the top.
  5. Chill for at least 6 hours, then cut into bars.

Tip

Wipe the knife with a hot damp cloth between cuts for clean edges.

content.rendered:
Gulab jamun made with milk powder are easier than the traditional khoya version and just as soft. Fry them slowly so they cook all the way through.

Prep: 20 min · Cook: 20 min · Serves: 20 pieces

Ingredients

  • 1 cup milk powder
  • 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1/4 tsp baking soda
  • 2 tbsp ghee
  • 4 to 5 tbsp milk
  • 1 1/2 cups sugar
  • 1 1/2 cups water
  • 4 cardamom pods, crushed
  • 1 tsp rose water
  • Oil for frying

Method

  1. Boil the sugar, water and cardamom for 5 minutes. Turn off the heat and add the rose water.
  2. Mix the milk powder, flour and baking soda. Rub in the ghee.
  3. Add milk a spoon at a time to make a soft, smooth dough. Rest 5 minutes.
  4. Roll into small crack-free balls.
  5. Fry on low heat, stirring gently, until deep golden brown, about 6 minutes.
  6. Drop the hot jamuns into the warm syrup and soak for at least 1 hour.

Tip

If the oil is too hot, the outside browns before the inside cooks. Low and slow is the rule.

content.rendered:
Everything you love about a mango lassi, frozen on a stick. Use ripe Alphonso mangoes if you can find them, or good canned mango pulp.

Prep: 10 min · Cook: 6 hours freezing · Serves: 8 popsicles

Ingredients

  • 2 cups ripe mango, chopped (or mango pulp)
  • 1 cup thick plain yoghurt
  • 2 tbsp honey
  • A pinch of cardamom powder

Method

  1. Blend the mango, yoghurt, honey and cardamom until smooth.
  2. Taste and add more honey if your mangoes are not very sweet.
  3. Pour into popsicle moulds and add sticks.
  4. Freeze for at least 6 hours. Run the moulds under warm water to release.

Tip

Leave a little space at the top of each mould. The mix expands as it freezes.

content.rendered:
The secret to the crackly top is whisking the sugar and eggs hard for a full minute. The secret to fudgy middles is taking them out of the oven a little early.

Prep: 15 min · Cook: 25 min · Serves: 16 squares

Ingredients

  • 200 g dark chocolate
  • 150 g butter
  • 1 1/4 cups sugar
  • 3 eggs
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 3/4 cup all-purpose flour
  • 1/4 cup cocoa powder
  • 1/2 tsp salt

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 20 cm square tin.
  2. Melt the chocolate and butter together, then cool for 5 minutes.
  3. Whisk the sugar, eggs and vanilla hard for 1 minute until pale.
  4. Whisk in the chocolate mix, then fold in the flour, cocoa and salt.
  5. Bake 22 to 25 minutes until the centre is just set. Cool completely before cutting.

Tip

Cool the brownies fully, even overnight, for clean squares.

This salad is made for meal prep. Chickpeas soak up the lemony dressing and the vegetables stay crunchy for days.

Prep: 15 min · Cook: 0 min · Serves: 4

Ingredients

  • 2 cans (400 g each) chickpeas, drained
  • 1 cucumber, diced
  • 2 tomatoes, diced
  • 1/2 red onion, finely chopped
  • 1/2 cup olives, halved
  • 100 g feta, crumbled
  • 3 tbsp olive oil
  • 2 tbsp lemon juice
  • 1 tsp dried oregano
  • Salt and pepper

Method

  1. Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
  2. Add the chickpeas and toss to coat.
  3. Add the cucumber, tomato, onion and olives.
  4. Top with feta just before serving.

Tip

If packing for later, keep the feta separate so it stays creamy.

All the flavour of restaurant paneer tikka, made in a frying pan and rolled into a wrap you can take to work.

Prep: 15 min · Cook: 10 min · Serves: 2

Ingredients

  • 200 g paneer, cubed
  • 3 tbsp thick yoghurt
  • 1 tsp tikka masala
  • 1/2 tsp red chilli powder
  • 1 tsp lemon juice
  • 1 red onion, sliced
  • 2 tortillas or rotis
  • 3 tbsp mint chutney
  • 1 tbsp oil

Method

  1. Mix the yoghurt, tikka masala, chilli powder, lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Coat the paneer.
  2. Heat the oil in a pan on high heat and sear the paneer until charred on all sides.
  3. Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
  4. Spread mint chutney on each tortilla, add the paneer and onion, and roll tightly.
  5. Cut in half and serve, or wrap in foil to pack.

Tip

Pat the paneer dry before marinating so the marinade sticks.

Biryani looks hard but it is really three simple steps: marinate the chicken, par-boil the rice, then layer and steam. This version works in any heavy pot.

Prep: 30 min · Cook: 45 min · Serves: 4

Ingredients

  • 500 g chicken, bone-in pieces
  • 1 cup plain yoghurt
  • 2 tbsp biryani masala
  • 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
  • 2 cups basmati rice, soaked 30 minutes
  • 2 onions, thinly sliced and fried
  • A pinch of saffron in 3 tbsp warm milk
  • Mint and coriander leaves
  • 3 tbsp ghee
  • Salt to taste

Method

  1. Marinate the chicken with yoghurt, biryani masala, ginger-garlic paste and salt for at least 30 minutes.
  2. Cook the chicken in a heavy pot with 1 tbsp ghee for 15 minutes until almost done.
  3. Boil the rice in salted water for 6 minutes until 70% cooked, then drain.
  4. Layer the rice over the chicken. Top with fried onions, herbs, saffron milk and the remaining ghee.
  5. Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes. Rest 5 minutes before opening.

Tip

Seal the lid with foil so no steam escapes. Steam is what cooks the top layer of rice.

Canned tomatoes make this soup possible any time of year. A little butter and cream round out the acidity and fresh basil makes it taste like summer.

Prep: 10 min · Cook: 20 min · Serves: 4

Ingredients

  • 2 tbsp butter
  • 1 onion, chopped
  • 3 garlic cloves, sliced
  • 2 cans (400 g each) whole tomatoes
  • 2 cups vegetable stock
  • 1 tsp sugar
  • 1/2 cup cream
  • A handful of fresh basil
  • Salt and pepper

Method

  1. Melt the butter in a pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
  2. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
  3. Add the tomatoes, stock and sugar. Simmer for 15 minutes.
  4. Blend until smooth, then stir in the cream and basil.
  5. Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

Tip

The soup freezes well for up to 3 months. Freeze it before adding the cream.

Good avocado toast is all about contrast: crunchy bread, creamy avocado, a squeeze of lime and an egg yolk that runs over everything.

Prep: 5 min · Cook: 5 min · Serves: 2

Ingredients

  • 2 thick slices sourdough bread
  • 1 ripe avocado
  • 1/2 lime, juiced
  • Pinch of chilli flakes
  • 2 eggs
  • 1 tsp vinegar
  • Salt and black pepper

Method

  1. Toast the bread until deep golden.
  2. Mash the avocado with lime juice, salt and pepper.
  3. Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar.
  4. Crack each egg into a cup, stir the water into a gentle swirl and slide the egg in. Cook 3 minutes.
  5. Spread the avocado on the toast, top with the egg and finish with chilli flakes.

Tip

The fresher the egg, the neater it poaches.

Overnight oats are the easiest healthy breakfast there is. Mix everything in a jar before bed and breakfast is waiting for you in the fridge.

Prep: 5 min · Cook: 0 min (overnight soak) · Serves: 1

Ingredients

  • 1/2 cup rolled oats
  • 1/2 cup milk
  • 1/4 cup plain yoghurt
  • 1 tbsp chia seeds
  • 1 tsp honey
  • 1/2 cup mixed berries

Method

  1. Add the oats, milk, yoghurt, chia seeds and honey to a jar.
  2. Stir well, close the lid and refrigerate overnight or at least 4 hours.
  3. In the morning, stir again and add a splash of milk if it is too thick.
  4. Top with berries and serve cold.

Tip

Use rolled oats, not instant oats. Instant oats turn mushy overnight.

This is the omelette sold at street stalls all over India, usually tucked inside soft buttered bread. It takes ten minutes and wakes you up better than coffee.

Prep: 5 min · Cook: 5 min · Serves: 1

Ingredients

  • 3 eggs
  • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • 1 small tomato, finely chopped
  • 1 green chilli, finely chopped
  • 2 tbsp chopped coriander
  • 1/4 tsp turmeric
  • 1/4 tsp red chilli powder
  • Salt to taste
  • 1 tbsp butter or oil

Method

  1. Beat the eggs with turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
  2. Stir in the onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander.
  3. Heat butter in a pan over medium heat and pour in the egg mix.
  4. Cook until the bottom is set, about 2 minutes, then flip or fold.
  5. Cook 1 more minute and serve hot with toast.

Tip

Keep the vegetables finely chopped so the omelette holds together when you fold it.

content.rendered:
These are the pancakes we make every Sunday. Buttermilk makes them tender and helps them rise tall, and resting the batter for five minutes gives you the fluffiest stack.

Prep: 5 min · Cook: 15 min · Serves: 4

Ingredients

  • 2 cups all-purpose flour
  • 2 tbsp sugar
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 2 cups buttermilk
  • 2 eggs
  • 3 tbsp melted butter, plus more for the pan

Method

  1. Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
  2. In another bowl whisk the buttermilk, eggs and melted butter.
  3. Pour the wet mix into the dry mix and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine.
  4. Rest the batter for 5 minutes while you heat a buttered pan over medium heat.
  5. Pour 1/4 cup of batter per pancake. Flip when bubbles form on top, about 2 minutes, then cook 1 minute more.

Tip

No buttermilk? Stir 2 tbsp lemon juice into 2 cups of milk and wait 5 minutes.
